event_id_observation.derivation: Confirmed in code and by recomputation. request_id = uuid5(REQUEST_NAMESPACE, idempotency_key) (src/reviewer_portal/data.py:61). event_id = uuid5(request_id, kind), with kind 'created', 'routed', 'decision' or 'classification:<attempt>' (data.py:259-266, event_id_for). uuid5(UUID('6ba15846-6243-50a8-bc03-82097efc7cd8'), 'decision') = 1337f128-8dff-5b2c-8410-28bbf7249c60.
event_id_observation.what_was_seen: The 2026-11-09 decision on 9797472 has the same request_id and decision event_id as the 2026-11-08 decision on the same award. The owner attests the 2026-11-08 action-log line at 2026-11-08T19:25:30.685463Z, with a different session_id. The warehouse row at review_requests v326 has the 2026-11-08 decision_at 19:25:26.384Z and rationale 'yes this ok to go forward'; the 2026-11-09 rationale differs.
event_id_observation.why_not_a_defect: Deterministic ids are the idempotency design: a retried submit or decision cannot create a second row. The two rows never coexisted: the first was deleted 2026-11-08 19:42:10Z, the second written 2026-11-09 17:55:09Z.
event_id_observation.consequence: Two distinct human actions, on different days in different sessions, share one audit event id. In the event table they differ only by timestamp (and the free-text rationale), because session and signed-in user live only in the app log. An event id identifies a (request, kind) pair, not an act. Telling the acts apart needs the at timestamp or Delta version, joined to the app log.
